title: Example 127 (B9) re-run: its statement says it is not vacuous, and that the records' constructors are another obligation
description: Step 2b of llm-dlc/loops/sound-verdicts.md makes vacuity a status of every verified statement (non-vacuous, vacuous or unknown, with how it is known), kept in result.stated.vacuity and stated on the page, and has the console and the statement say, for a proof over records built through their constructors, that whether the two versions' constructors accept the same inputs is not part of the proof. Example 127 (Crosscut's Backoff#delayMillis, a record method, proved equal by JBMC) is the recorded proof over records: its harness skips an input a constructor rejects, so the tool's own checker probes it, and the result should record status non-vacuous with the probe's witness (a delayMillis(this=Backoff[...], attempt=...) call), the constructors' caveat among the assumptions, and the same verified verdict as before. Nothing about the proof itself changed.
expected: verified, matching expected; result.stated.vacuity.status non-vacuous with basis probe and a witness; a constructible assumption in result.stated.assumptions; the page's 'What the verdict is about' paragraph ends with the witness sentence
